clue.text: Pop singer having good range?

parts.note: an Aga is a make of kitchen range, a large cast-iron cooker

explanation.surface: A question about whether a chart star has a good vocal range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a singer's compass of notes, but it is the cooker: an AGA is a heavy British stove found in country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Gaga is a famous pop star, known widely by her surname alone.

clue.text: One who sells very little scrap gold

parts.note: an end is a small leftover piece, as in odds and ends
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A trader who flogs tiny bits of scrap gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendor is a seller, the trader in any sale.

clue.text: Desperate attempt to survive Skegness?

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure
Skegness is a seaside resort on the Lincolnshire coast

explanation.surface: A quip that it takes desperation to endure a holiday in Skegness.
explanation.walkthrough: Skegness is a traditional English seaside holiday town, so it stands for RESORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A last resort is the final desperate measure tried when everything else has failed.

clue.text: Republican rule upset American creature

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word rule and the Republican letter upside down, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: a rule is a law
US means American

explanation.surface: A political tale of an American Republican overturning a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'upset' means turned upside down, so the letters read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: The walrus is a large tusked marine mammal, so a creature.

clue.text: See great changes in economy travel

indicators.note: great changes says the letters undergo a change of order, a rearrangement of the fodder

explanation.surface: An observation that budget travel has altered greatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, the budget way to travel.

clue.text: Crack all right in aeroplane losing tail

indicators.note: in tells us the all-right letters are placed inside the shortened plane
losing its tail means the plane word drops its final letter

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone cracks a joke on board a plane that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like damage to the stricken plane, but it is a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, a quip.

clue.text: Indiscreet embrace involving the French

indicators.note: involving means the embrace word wraps round the French article

parts.note: a caress is a fond embrace or stroke
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: An indiscreet cuddle with a French person.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless talk is unguarded, revealing what should be kept quiet.

clue.text: Resolution in Hamlet for example

definitions.meaning: a hamlet is a small ..., a village

explanation.surface: A literary question about how Hamlet is resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital H makes us think of Shakespeare's prince, but it is a small village.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement is both an agreed resolution and an inhabited place such as a hamlet.

clue.text: Stadium accommodating any number in region

indicators.note: accommodating means the region word holds the number letter inside it

parts.note: an area is a region
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A stadium in a region with room for any number of people.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a sports ground or stadium with seating around it.

clue.text: Help with navigation? Boats are wrecked crossing lake!

indicators.note: crossing means the rearranged boat letters go across, around, the lake letter
wrecked signals the words boats are are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: L abbreviates lake on maps

explanation.surface: A plea for navigational help after boats are wrecked on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' shuffles BOATS ARE; 'crossing' puts it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an old instrument sailors used to find latitude from the stars.

clue.text: Might this professional be called to account?

definitions.text: Might this professional be called to account?

parts.words: Might this professional be called to account?
parts.note: being called to account usually means being blamed; here the professional is literally called in to examine accounts

explanation.surface: A question whether some professional will be held responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is the accountant brought in to inspect a firm's books.

clue.text: Group in most natural surroundings

definitions.meaning: an ... is a group within a larger body, as in the criminal ...
to be where one is most at home

explanation.surface: A group of people found in their most natural setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Element covers both a section of people and the habitat one thrives in.

clue.text: Concede match

explanation.definitionFit: Agreeing both admits a point and corresponds, as figures that tally.

clue.text: Defendant keeping male cat as familiar

indicators.note: keeping means the defendant word holds the cat inside it

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A defendant who keeps a tomcat as a witch's familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'familiar' teases a witch's cat, but means used to, as in familiar with.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed to something means used to it, well acquainted with it.

clue.text: Deep breath?

parts.note: the deep is the sea, and a breath of air from it is a light wind off the water

explanation.definitionFit: A sea breeze is a wind blowing inland off the ocean, the deep.

clue.text: Orangeries falling into disrepair? Shake up needed!

indicators.note: a building falling into disrepair crumbles apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Neglected glasshouses on an estate call for an overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling into disrepair' shuffles ORANGERIES, all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake up an organisation is to restructure it, to arrange it anew.

clue.text: Sweet sauce, almost cold, with some hot bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go mad and are rearranged
almost means the word cold loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A dessert of bananas with a nearly cold sauce and some hot ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts COLD to COL; 'bananas' shuffles SAUCE, COL, SOME and HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate mousse is a light whipped pudding, a dessert or sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Please! Write down scheme for avoiding partition!

parts.note: O is an old exclamation of entreaty, as in O, please
to pen is to write down
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A frantic plea to record a plan for avoiding the division of a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partition' suggests dividing a nation, but means internal walls.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office or home has no dividing walls between areas.

clue.text: Main article on redesigned trailer

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: redesigned means the word trailer is reworked into a new letter order

explanation.surface: The lead article on a redesigned film trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road or route is a main one, like a major artery.

clue.text: Witness putting Murphy on spot for hearing?

indicators.note: for hearing says the words are judged by how they sound spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a murphy is slang for a potato, a tater, put after a speck, a spot

explanation.surface: Someone putting a man named Murphy on the spot at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato (from the Irish staple), TATER; on SPECK makes SPECK TATER, said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker who sees something happen, as a witness does.

clue.text: Severe reprimand given in space vehicle

definitions.meaning: British slang for a stern telling-off

explanation.surface: An astronaut given a dressing-down inside their spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting a rocket is British slang for being told off severely.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocket names both a sharp rebuke and a launch vehicle.

clue.text: Scotsman in good time finds mammoth

indicators.note: in places the Scotsman inside the good and time letters

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scot who arrives in good time finds a mammoth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth as an adjective means huge, enormous, of giant size.

clue.text: Actor Gardner on pitch in movie

parts.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star
pitch is tar, the black sticky substance

explanation.surface: A film star appearing on a pitch in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is a James Cameron blockbuster film.

clue.text: Propane volatile in theory

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the letters of propane are restless and rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist's claim that propane is volatile in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle, though maybe not in practice.

clue.text: Penniless pair keeping two ducks

indicators.note: keeping means the pair letters hold the ducks inside

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O, so two of them

explanation.surface: A broke couple still keeping two ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor means having little or no money.

clue.text: 5 amps put through container ship? Seek opinion

indicators.note: put through means the number and amps are pushed into the middle of the container and ship

parts.note: a can is a container
SS stands for steamship
V is five in Roman numerals
A is the symbol for amps

explanation.surface: An electrician's instruction to run five amps through a container ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to survey people's views, as before an election.

clue.text: Support second story having deleted one

indicators.note: having deleted means the numeral for one is dropped from the story word

parts.note: an item is a news story
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An editor backs a second story after cutting one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having deleted' removes I from ITEM, leaving TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem holds up a flower or leaf, so it is a supporting stalk.

clue.text: Nuts are able to expand

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the words are able to go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that nuts can swell in size.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to expand on something, adding detail.

clue.text: National Express

definitions.meaning: ... means of the nation, as in a ... occasion

explanation.surface: National Express, the name of a British coach company.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the name of National Express, a long-distance British coach operator.
explanation.definitionFit: State works both as the nation's own and as a verb for voicing something.
